## Statement

**Skorohod's Representation Theorem** shows that a sequence converging
[[convergence-in-law|in law]] can be represented by a sequence with the same
laws that converges **almost surely** on a common probability space. This lets
us prove statements about convergence in law using pointwise arguments.

:::{.theorem data-title="Skorohod's Representation Theorem"}

Suppose that $X_{n}\stackrel{\mathcal{D}}{\to}X$ as $n \to \infty$ with
$F_{n}(x):=\mathbb{P}(X_{n} \leq x)$ and $F(x):=\mathbb{P}(X\leq x)$ for
$x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then there exists a probability space
$(\Omega', \mathcal{F}',\mathbb{P}')$ and random variables $\{Y_{n}, n\geq 1\}$
and $Y$ on it such that
$$
Y_{n}\stackrel{\mathcal{D}}{=}X_{n}\ \text{ for every } n,\qquad Y\stackrel{\mathcal{D}}{=}X,
$$
and $Y_{n}\stackrel{a.s.}{\to}Y$ as $n \to \infty$.

:::

## Skorohod's Construction

Take $\Omega'=(0,1)$, $\mathcal{F}'=\mathcal{B}((0,1))$ and $\mathbb{P}'$ the
Lebesgue measure, $\mathbb{P}'((a,b])=b-a$. For $\omega \in \Omega'$ define the
generalised inverses
$$
Y_n(\omega):= \inf\{  x: \omega \leq F_{n}(x)\},\qquad Y(\omega):= \inf\{  x: \omega \leq F(x) \}.
$$
By right-continuity of distribution functions,
$$
\omega \leq  F_{n}(x) \iff Y_{n}(\omega)\leq  x,\qquad
\omega \leq  F(x) \iff Y(\omega)\leq  x,
$$
hence
$$
\mathbb{P}'(Y_{n}\leq  y)  =\mathbb{P}'(\omega \leq  F_{n}(y)) =F_{n}(y),\qquad
\mathbb{P}'(Y\leq  y)= F(y).
$$
So $Y_n$ has the law of $X_n$ and $Y$ the law of $X$.

:::{.proof}

It remains to show $Y_{n}\to Y$ a.s. Note that $Y$ and each $Y_n$ are
non-decreasing in $\omega$. Recall that $X_n\Rightarrow X$ means
$F_n(x)\to F(x)$ at every continuity point $x$ of $F$, and these points are
dense in $\mathbb{R}$. Fix $\omega\in(0,1)$.

*Lower bound.* Let $x<Y(\omega)$ be a continuity point of $F$. Then
$F(x)<\omega$, so $F_n(x)<\omega$ for all large $n$, which means
$Y_n(\omega)>x$. Hence $\liminf_n Y_n(\omega)\geq x$, and letting
$x\uparrow Y(\omega)$ gives $\liminf_n Y_n(\omega)\geq Y(\omega)$.

*Upper bound.* Let $\omega<\omega'<1$ and let $y>Y(\omega')$ be a continuity
point of $F$. Then $F(y)\geq\omega'>\omega$, so $F_n(y)>\omega$ for all large
$n$, so $Y_n(\omega)\leq y$. Hence $\limsup_n Y_n(\omega)\leq y$, and letting
$y\downarrow Y(\omega')$ gives $\limsup_n Y_n(\omega)\leq Y(\omega')$.

If $\omega$ is a continuity point of $Y$, letting $\omega'\downarrow\omega$ gives
$\limsup_n Y_n(\omega)\leq Y(\omega)$, so $Y_n(\omega)\to Y(\omega)$. As $Y$ is
monotone it has at most countably many discontinuities, a Lebesgue-null set,
so $Y_n\to Y$ $\mathbb{P}'$-almost surely.

:::

## Application

:::{.proposition data-title="Bounded Continuous Test Functions"}

If $X_{n}\stackrel{\mathcal{D}}{\to}X$ and $\varphi$ is bounded and continuous,
then
$$
\lim_{n\to \infty}\mathbb{E}[\varphi(X_{n})]=\mathbb{E}[\varphi(X)].
$$

:::

:::{.proof}

With $Y_n,Y$ as above, $\varphi(Y_n)\to\varphi(Y)$ a.s. by continuity, and
$|\varphi(Y_n)|\leq\sup|\varphi|<\infty$. By the
[[dominated-convergence-theorem]],
$\mathbb{E}\varphi(X_n)=\mathbb{E}\varphi(Y_n)\to\mathbb{E}\varphi(Y)=\mathbb{E}\varphi(X)$.

:::
